quest.title: Competition on the Sands
quest.description: The Interdarshan Championship has entered the second round. This round takes place in the desert. Head to the Aaru Village sub-venue to see how things are going...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: A Parade of Providence: Act II
chapter.title: Beginnings and Endings

talks.objective: Go to the sub-venue in Aaru Village

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Um, is it me, or are the bags under your eyes even darker than during the last round? Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Thanks for the concern, Kaveh. I just... haven't been sleeping well lately...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Even though I try to fall asleep, I can't get the Championship out of my head... and before I know it, it's morning again.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* I know the feeling. That happens to me too when I'm agonizing over my blueprints.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Do you have any tips for dealing with that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: To be honest with you, no. You could say there are many things that don't have a quick fix, and can only be endured.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmm, I suppose you can think of it as something akin to an illness. Sometimes there's no effective cure, so you just have to let things run their course.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I don't know what's stressing you out, but I can feel all the anxiety and pressure coming from you. The next round's about to start, so chin up and do your best.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, okay... You do your best, too.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Looks like everyone's here. I will now explain the second round to you all.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There are three Ley Line Disruptors buried in the area around Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: These devices can imitate the effects of Ley Line disruption and will constantly interfere with the environment. Your goal is to shut them down.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The first three who manage to finish this task will be awarded four, three, and two points, accordingly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Note that each person may only bring a set amount of food and water with them, and that leaving the designated competition zone will result in disqualification.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, what do you think? Want to team up again?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I shall consider letting you have the points on account of what happened in the previous round.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's alright. I've been here many times, and in any case, machines are one of my specialties. I doubt this will be particularly difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It's good to see such confidence in a youngster like yourself. I also happen to be well acquainted with this place. Let's see who will find these devices first.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But aside from us, you should remember that there's a favorite for champion. We must be careful of him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A favorite to win? Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Shh, not so loud. I mean that boy, Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: He took first place in the previous round, and if he does so again this time, we may as well declare this competition over.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I heard that you solved the Avidya Forest's Ley Line effluence problem with him not long ago. Since this round involves resolving a machine-simulated Ley Line disruption, it should be a simple matter for him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's true. It does look like his odds of winning are pretty high!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: He already has Collei, who is an excellent pupil. If he were to win this round as well, then wouldn't we just be letting him have all the fun?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: As his senior, it's my solemn duty to prevent such an inequitable arrangement from happening. I'm off!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'll get going as well. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...How are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I think I'm okay. But I'll take things slowly for now.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Is this all the water we're getting?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Sorry, that's what the rules say...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: While this round seems to be about how quickly you can shut down the devices, it's also testing your ability to survive in tough conditions.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I knew it'd be harder than I had expected.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: So we'll either need to find the devices as quickly as possible, or we'll have to save our energy and wait for an opportunity... Okay, I'll head out shortly. Thanks a lot, Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You're welcome. Please take care of yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, there goes everybody.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, who should we visit this time? Let Paimon think...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! Didn't Faruzan say that Tighnari's the favorite to win? Let's go look for him first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, hey, Tighnari! Tighnariii!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird, the locator says that he should be around here somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari! Can you hear us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right! Oh no, it looks like he's fainted. We have to help him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's... so hot...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you passed out because of the heat! Are you not used to getting around in the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's right... I usually bring lots of water when I go to the desert, precisely to avoid this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I went through all my water very quickly, and with the effects of the disturbed Ley Lines, I started feeling dizzy.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My ancestors, the Valuka Shuna, were originally from the desert. But I guess this is what happens when a species migrates — they become intolerant of their original environment...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This isn't the time for a history lesson. Let's get you some water—

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Humans, such fragile beings. Your bodies can't even survive extreme changes in the environment.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Here, take this. Let him drink it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you serious? This had better be just normal water... Hey! You're leaving already?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It seems it really is just water.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon really doesn't get that guy... What's he up to? Anyway, let's focus on helping Tighnari drink some water first...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tighnari starts to recover after getting some water...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'm feeling a little better now. Thanks, you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it wasn't just the two of us. Just now—

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Found you at last.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cyno! You're here too!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I was concerned, so I came back to check on you. Will you be able to go on?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The fur on my tail is so dry it's practically been singed right off. I don't see any purpose in pushing myself beyond what is reasonable.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It appears I'm not suited to this particular round — I should probably just return to Aaru Village and rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? So you're backing out?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Yes. I do have my results in the first round to serve as a buffer, so even if I forfeit this round, I still have a chance to turn things around later.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Withdrawing now will allow me to conserve my energy. Continuing to push onward would be counterproductive.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: A wise decision. Let's get you back to Aaru Village.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ugh... It's fine, I can make it back on my own...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, stop trying to be so polite. Come on, we'll help you back to Aaru Village!

talks.objective: Bring Tighnari back so he can rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are you feeling now, Tighnari? Do you want to rest some more?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's some shade here, so we can stop for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, let's do that.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: #Oh, Cyno and Tighnari... and you've got {NICKNAME} and Paimon with you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey Layla!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah, the sun was too strong, so I decided to take cover here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: What about you? Are you all done already?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Unfortunately not. I'm not quite as capable as I thought... I intend to withdraw from this round. Cyno and {NICKNAME} are escorting me back to Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: W—Withdraw? Can you even do that?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I believe the rules do provide for such a situation. Alhaitham did say that the act of leaving the competition grounds would result in disqualification from the round.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Didn't I ask you if you were alright before this? If you had just decided to withdraw then, you wouldn't have had to suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, I had to try, didn't I? So I tried, and it didn't work out — and now I'm backing out while I can.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: When I get back, I'm definitely going to make a batch of sun-resistant oil. Next time I venture into the desert, I'll be prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: By the way, you're Layla, aren't you? You don't look very well yourself. Will you be alright?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I did feel a little faint when I first entered the desert, but I feel a lot better after resting here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Be careful not to push yourself too hard!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm just...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Feeling the pressure?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Huh? You can tell?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Your expression is similar to the ones I see on criminals' faces when I interrogate them.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: To tell you the truth, I'm still not sure whether I have what it takes to represent the Rtawahist Darshan in the Championship.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Most people voted for me because of all the rumors surrounding me, and to be honest, those rumors don't really mean anything. Now I don't know how to deal with all the expectations they've put on me.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Even the people who usually criticize me voted for me this time... So I feel like I have to live up to their expectations somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So their expectations are putting pressure on you?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yes. Actually, I heard that you were voted in as well, Tighnari. How do you deal with it?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: To be completely honest, I don't really feel any pressure.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Firstly, those who expect things from you do not necessarily do so for benign reasons. On the other hand, those who do consider your feelings certainly wouldn't want you to push yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Next, we are researchers. Our primary duty is to interact with knowledge, not to meet others' expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As for me, I took part in this competition to advertise for an academic lecture at Gandharva Ville next month. I'll obviously try my best during the competition, but I won't let any additional pressure get to me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I think you can also try to find a clearly defined goal. That may help you.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I understand. Thanks for your advice.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Phew... I'm absolutely parched after talking so much.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I've still got some water with me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No, I'll be alright. We aren't far from Aaru Village, so I can go the rest of the way myself. You should get back to the competition. Don't you want to win that limited-edition card?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. Alright then, your spirit will live on through me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Hey, don't talk like that. I'm not dead, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Everyone, I'll be heading back now. See you after the round ends.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll continue searching for the Ley Line Disruptors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you feeling better now, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah. I feel like some of the weight has been taken off my shoulders after chatting with Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: It's been a long time since I first left my hometown to come to the Akademiya, and every day here has been so precious... But of course, there have been some tough times.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: All sorts of complex astrological models, countless quizzes, and essays that took all my brainpower to barely finish... Each of those things are like huge boulders barreling at me, forcing me to continue running forward.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: When I was chosen as my Darshan's representative, it felt like another boulder was added to the ones already rolling behind me. Every time I close my eyes, I think of all the people I'd disappoint if I mess up.

choices.text: We would never be disappointed in you.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Yeah, I think that's what Tighnari was trying to tell me.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: You're our good friends, which is why you didn't stop him from dropping out of this round, and why you don't feel disappointed in me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! No need to feel so down!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: That said, he did also say that he hopes I could have more concrete goals for taking part in this competition. I don't have any now, but I'll give that some thought.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Anyway, I won't take up any more of your time. You still have to record the other contestants' progress, don't you? Perhaps they've had some breakthroughs while we've been chatting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, we should go look for the others. Hmm, now who's left? Tighnari's dropped out for the round, and we just saw Cyno...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: You could go see how Madam Faruzan's doing. I've heard that she's quite knowledgeable about the desert, so she's probably made some progress by now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Let's go look for Faruzan!

choices.text: We'd prefer you to be happy, Layla.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Faruzan. Have you made any progress?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah, you're just in time. I'm about to start digging right here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you found the Ley Line Disruptor already?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmph, such a simple problem could never confound me.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Not long after entering the desert, I discovered a Primal Construct that was acting abnormally, so I followed it all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Once I got near here, it suddenly disappeared. Something unusual must be happening around this area.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're a true expert, Madam Faruzan! You knew what to do right away!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, I do happen to have more experience than most. But that aside, has anyone completed this challenge yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, not yet!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well then, I suppose I'll be the first. What about that boy Tighnari?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He withdrew from this round.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oh, and why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's not used to being out and about in the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Huh, I didn't think he would have such a weakness. I suppose he could use a bit more training.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What about the others? Is that Rtawahist girl still a bundle of nerves?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari gave Layla some advice, and she seems to be doing a lot better now. Cyno just started his search for the Disruptors, and as for Hat Guy... Well, who knows what he's thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: And what about Kaveh? Has he found a Ley Line Disruptor yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't think so, or our locators would've already let us know.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Strange, what's he lollygagging for? With his skills, you should've heard something from him by now.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, I'm afraid the most thrilling moments are already done here. You should probably go find Kaveh and see how he's faring now.

talks.objective: Observe and record the circumstances surrounding Kaveh

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Come on, stop following me! I already gave you all the food I had on me.

dialogues.speaker: Desert Fox
dialogues.text: *whine*

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You can cry all you want. I don't have any more food! All I have left is half a bottle of water, and I can't possibly give you that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Without water, traveling in the desert will be incredibly difficult, and I still need to find what I'm looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Mehrak, can you help me out here? Keep them away!

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh, there you are!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Faruzan told us to come see how you're doing. What are you up to?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* Just thinking about it makes me upset. Not long after I entered the desert, I was accosted by these fellows.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I don't know why, but they didn't leave the competition grounds, and now the Ley Line disruptions have left them confused and circling around the area.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The moment they saw me, they wouldn't leave me alone. They even cheated me out of my limited food supply.

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Desert Fox
dialogues.text: *whine*

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hey, didn't I ask you to keep them away?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh, is this flying metal thingy yours?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's right. This is my toolbox, Mehrak.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your toolbox? It seems pretty fancy... Uh... Hey there, can you understand us?

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why's it here with you?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sometimes I need to carry things when I go out, so it's handy to have a portable toolbox.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, this definitely doesn't look like an ordinary toolbox, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's a long story. When I was working in the desert, I ran into a merchant group who had a machine core they excavated from some tomb.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It was clearly from King Deshret's civilization. His technology still isn't fully understood, and Kshahrewar has many different opinions on this topic.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Our current theories cannot explain such mysteries. Upon seeing such a rare, complete specimen before me, I forked over all the Mora on my person to purchase it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Some time back, I wanted to make an automated case that could store my offloaded items. With that core, I created Mehrak.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It can't understand commands that are too complex, but it can serve as my assistant and help me with things like mapping and surveying.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Most importantly, it can't talk, so it can't give me any attitude.

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, yes — thanks for helping hide the fact that I live at Alhaitham's place earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon was the one who gave it away in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* I hope this season of my life ends soon, so I can get things back on track.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Things just... started going downhill at some point. Maybe it all started when my mom remarried and left for Fontaine. Or maybe it all started when I spoke to Alhaitham in the library...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Or maybe it's because constructing the Palace of Alcazarzaray burned through my funds. I'm still paying off the debt from that one... Argh, when's this going to end!?

dialogues.speaker: Desert Fox
dialogues.text: *whine*

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, I guess we're all unlucky here.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's not like any of you asked to be trapped in a Ley Line disruption... Okay, let me get you all out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh, aren't you going to look for the Ley Line Disruptors?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yes, but I can't just leave them here, can I?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, forget it. The more I think about this, the more I feel a headache coming on. I'll get back to searching once I get them out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Time's a-wasting — I'm off!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh looks like he's conflicted... He really wants to win, but he can't ignore those he wants to help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's always felt like he's the type who easily gets himself into tough spots.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon doesn't mean this in an insulting way, but... he seems like the kind of guy who'd be really easy to take advantage of.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're certainly cruel with the truth...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah, someone's done already!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? Wonder who it is. Let's go back and ask Alhaitham!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon also wants to know! Let's go back and ask Alhaitham!

choices.text: He can only do one or the other...

talks.objective: Return to the Aaru Village sub-venue

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Verification complete! Congratulations on being this round's first winner, Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so Cyno was the quickest!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I am from Spantamad, after all. We know a lot about Ley Lines, so finding a disruptor was never going to be particularly difficult for me.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #Since {NICKNAME} and Paimon also happen to be here... Do you have anything you want to say?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Anything I want to say...? My friend couldn't continue on, so failure was never an option.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: "The bonds of yesterday will forge the road to tomorrow. With the ties of friendship that bind us, I won't lose to anyone."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...That's a line from "King of Invokations," one of my favorite works, and it sums up my thoughts right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It might be a good thing that Tighnari isn't here, or else he'd give Cyno a good smack right about now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's so Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh wow, it's already so late. Everyone's probably running low on food and water — it'll only get harder from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Something similar happened in "King of Invokations." What a classic.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Any thoughts on that, Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I have no thoughts regarding "King of Invokations."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou obviously wasn't asking about that!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Deserts are much more dangerous at night, so this competition should be nearing its end. At the moment, only Faruzan, Layla, and Kaveh remain.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I wonder who the next person to find a disruptor will be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, only three people are left? Tighnari forfeited, and Cyno's already done... What about Hat Guy?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: He also forfeited not long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't understand what he's thinking at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But like Alhaitham said — the round's almost over. Let's go see what the other contestants are doing!

talks.objective: Observe and record the circumstances of other competitors

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Hello again... You know, it suddenly occurred to me that you guys have had to do a lot of running around this time. Don't you find it tiring?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Really? Wow. I dunno where you get your strength from...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: The desert's getting colder now that night's falling. And the wind can really sting your face because of all the sand in it.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Has anyone finished this round yet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cyno's already shut one down. Have you made any progress yet?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I circled the whole area, but I didn't find anything.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: But I did have the chance to think some more about that thing that was weighing on my mind, and I realized something.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And what was that?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Well, my fellow Rtawahist members must have all put my name forward for different reasons. And maybe a lot of them only picked me because they wanted to watch me make a fool of myself.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: But be that as it may, I believe that a lot of them genuinely do expect great things from me.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: And I want to live up to their expectations. I don't want them to regret putting my name down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But doesn't thinking like that put a lot of pressure on you?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Of course, that comes with some amount of pressure, for sure. But now I've thought about it, I don't feel like this is something I have to do. Instead, it's something I want to do.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: That may not sound like a huge difference to you. But it's helped me relax a lot... so don't worry about me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's great!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Also, now that I've relaxed... I'm suddenly really sleepy...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I think I'll just... take a quick nap... just a quick one...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Hmm? But the competition isn't over yet... Oh, Layla, Layla... she's really a bundle of nerves, isn't she?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're...!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Good to see you too. Whew, it's nice to be out — feels like I've been cooped up inside for quite a while.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Well, since I'm here, I guess I should help her finish this. What are we supposed to be doing here again? Finding a Ley Line Disruptor, was it?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Let me see... Hmm, looks like she's basically gathered all the information she needs. It won't take long to wrap this up.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Come with me, you two.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Well, in that case, let's take a short breather here.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Ah, this should be it, right? I'll turn it off — that should restore the Ley Lines in the area to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice work!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Again, I didn't do any of the real work. I'm just wrapping up.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: She'll probably wake up soon... No doubt she'll be a little disoriented at first, but once she's got her bearings, she'll go and report that she shut down this disruptor.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Will you be staying here for a while? Or are you going to check on the other contestants?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Time to check our locator... Whoa! It looks like Kaveh and Faruzan are heading toward the same place!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Perhaps they're about to find the last disruptor. ...Also, speaking of Kaveh, he's an interesting one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Before the second round, he had a chat with the other me. He said that worries can be like illnesses — they don't always have a magic cure. Sometimes, you just have to endure them as best you can until they run their course.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: But the way I see it, his situation is much worse than my other self's... She just hadn't found what she wanted to do at that moment, which is why she felt lost.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Kaveh, meanwhile, knows what he wants to do — he's convinced that he has to win — and yet, he still seems conflicted...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: He doesn't have a second personality, but... somehow, he still seems like he's at odds with himself in some way.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: ...I don't know exactly how to describe it. It's like he's smiling on the outside, but there's no joy inside. Only sorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Still, who knows. He must be more experienced than me — maybe he's just better at dealing with it all than I am.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, but back to the topic of wrapping up... Shouldn't you be getting back to the action to record how everything plays out? Last one, then the round's over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, true. Okay then, guess we'll be going now! We'll keep everything you said in mind!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It should be around here...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Finally found it...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Kaveh? Are you...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Madam Faruzan! And here I thought you would've finished this round by now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Faruzan, Kaveh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, looks like Layla's already done.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I didn't expect that you and I would find a disruptor at the same time... How are the other contestants doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari and Hat Guy forfeited, while Cyno and Layla are already done. You two are the only ones left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's weird. Didn't you start digging really early on?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Yes. I kept digging, but instead of finding a disruptor, I found a ruin.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I fell down pretty deep, and it was completely dark in there. It took me quite some time to unlock the various mechanisms and return to the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... actually really impressive...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Finishing a week's worth of trials in such a short time... That's pretty amazing, Madam Faruzan...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What about you? Why are you so late?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I encountered a lot of lost Desert Foxes along the way, and I brought them to the outskirts of the competition zone. When I came back, I was absolutely parched... and then I blacked out. Probably from the heat, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: When I woke up, it was already night. I used the last of my strength to come here.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: A most curious reason indeed... Ah, but are you sure you're alright? It sounds like you were in an incredibly dangerous situation.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: You said you were familiar with the desert, but the way you handle problems... It does feel rather at odds with your title as a genius.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ahaha, it was problematic, but that had nothing to do with me being a genius. It was my decision.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...The way I did things wasn't optimal, but I wouldn't have been comfortable not doing it, either. My conscience would've weighed on me.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. Youths these days, each stranger than the next.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But back to the main issue at hand. Since we're both very certain that this is where the final Ley Line Disruptor is, let's dig it up then.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Working together, the two unearth the final Ley Line Disruptor.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, this is indeed it, of that there is no doubt. But how should we count the score this time?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What is it, youngster? You seem relieved.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, nothing. I was just thinking that this round's finally over.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...There shouldn't be any more innocent creatures getting wrapped up in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: As for the points... I guess we can draw lots again later. I can't think of anything better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright. In that case, let's all head back to Aaru Village. Paimon thinks you'll both need some water and rest.

talks.objective: Return to the sub-venue and check the results of the competition

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Looks like the second round is over. I wonder who was faster, Kaveh or Madam Faruzan? ...Huh? Where's Madam Faruzan?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: She went to get water — she'll be back shortly. We basically arrived at the same time, so we'd like to draw lots again.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You get caught up in some things so easily — like drawing lots.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm not "caught up" in anything! Don't make it sound like I take pleasure in having bad luck!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Really? Then, should I say that you have a curious affinity for drawing lots?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Um, I'll go get the box and slips of paper for the lots. Please wait a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oho, here we go again. Let's see how I fare.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a brief but tense lot-drawing, Kaveh emerges triumphant...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I got it! Did you see that? I won!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Congratulations!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Kaveh's luck's taken a turn for the better!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Finally, after all this time... *sniff*

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It looks like you've been rewarded for your tribulations in the desert. This round's points are yours.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: And with that, our second round is done. Cyno, Layla, and Kaveh are our victorious contestants!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: As for the current standings, let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Cyno and Layla both have four points, putting them both in first place. The rest in descending order are Tighnari, Faruzan, Kaveh, and Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The next round will be the final one. Please rest up before then, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I heard that some stalls at the Wisdom Gala are debuting new games, so feel free to drop by if you're interested. Otherwise, see you next round!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: That boy knows a great deal — perhaps he might yet follow the trail of some desert creature to the devices.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Now that the round's begun, who do you think will win, Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The ones who find the disruptors will win.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Well, um, yes... but aren't you just repeating the rules?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I didn't expect Tighnari to drop out...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Being able to acknowledge one's own weaknesses is a rare quality.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Things are really heating up now! You can feel the contestants' passion too, can't you, Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Compared to the abstraction of human emotions, the desert heat is easier to intuit. Tighnari made the right decision to forfeit.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: This seems more annoying than the last round. That's fine, though — I'll find someplace to sit and watch them scurry.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The sun is especially intense today. I hope Tighnari will be alright.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: *sigh* Probably not. I should go check on him.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: *pants* I feel... a little faint...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Let me see. Where would they put one of these disruptors...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: A Desert Fox? Why would there be Desert Foxes here? Woah, stop biting my clothes! Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You two must have a lot of free time if you came looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: There's another one...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like someone's taking it easy!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You should be thrilled that I have nothing to do. Otherwise, that means someone's in for a very, very bad day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if you don't get any points this round, you won't have a shot at winning!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's not like I care about winning or clout. Really, the real prize for me is watching all these people fight over something so useless.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh, you've reminded me of something. There shouldn't be any more incidents after this round. If you'll excuse me, I have somewhere to be.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: "I will never give up..."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm, how did the rest go... Oh, right! "I will never give up! My will is my greatest weapon..."

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I think I'll start by doing a loop around the competition zone...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! Here it comes! I think I'm about to strike gold!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: There's a few things that seem a little off about this place. Lemme collect my thoughts for a second...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph, I see. Twenty years ago...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Much better. Aaru Village's hospitality sure is something... Two whole pitchers of water, to be precise.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If your throat's too wet as a result, I can provide some dry humor—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No, no thanks! Much appreciated, though.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Shh, quiet. I'm currently trying to find a way out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Desert Fox
dialogues.text: *whine*

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Plus, now that someone has shut one of the disruptors down, the contrast between before and after can provide me with further information still.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Let me see... It should be here, I think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh and Faruzan were super confident at the start, but it turns out they're the last ones to find a disruptor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But between the two of them, who's going to get there first? Let's head over, quick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How weird. The locator says that Madam Faruzan's nearby, but... where?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (I'm not sweating too much, am I? Oh, it'd be so embarrassing if that was caught on Kamera...)

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: (The weather today might affect this round.)
